discussion_comments.comment_body: Valid, fixed in 9623170f7. The refresh key now includes the user message count (`${status}:${users}:${tools}`), so a new turn always changes the key even without tool calls, and the previous turn's fetched changes can no longer count as current.

**[P2] Apply provisioning suppression to the combined loader condition.** On a new cloud send, `beginPendingResponse` sets the optimistic marker. The coordinator emits `cloud_provisioning` through the partial-message stream before the full-state acknowledgement arrives; partial messages leave `turnState` unchanged, and that acknowledgement goes through the 50 ms state-post debounce. During this handoff, `forceShow` is still true and the provisioning message has `partial: false`, so `optimisticShow` below overrides this `false` and renders “Thinking…” alongside the progress card. This contradicts the intended suppression and adds an avoidable loader insertion/removal at startup.

Gate the combined condition passed to `useDebouncedLoaderVisibility` on the provisioning tail, keeping the hook call unconditional. The added helper-only test misses this: rendering the full hook with a provisioning tail, stale idle `turnState`, and `forceShow: true` currently returns visible. Cover that combination, then verify an `api_req_started` successor can show the loader again.

Good catch, thanks. Fixed in f8d9ca206: the provisioning check now gates the combined condition passed to `useDebouncedLoaderVisibility` (`!cloudProvisioning && (optimisticShow || isWaitingForResponse || handoffToReasoningPending)`), and the hook call stays unconditional. I moved the check out of `computeIsWaitingForResponse` instead of duplicating it, so that helper matches main again.

I replaced the helper-only test with a full-hook test: a provisioning tail, a stale idle `turnState`, and `forceShow: true` keep the loader hidden, then an `api_req_started` successor shows it again. The test fails on the previous code (`expected true to be false`) and passes with the fix.

Valid, fixed in 90df99574b. `applyCanonicalHistory` now returns `withLivePluginIssues(sessionMessages, historyMessages)`, which carries the session's live plugin-warning lines (`meta.messageKind: "plugin_issue"`) into the saved history, each inserted at its original position by `createdAt`. It also skips any line whose id is already in history. Tests: the hook test now finishes a queued turn so the reconcile path replaces the transcript with saved history that has no warnings. It asserts the saved answer is applied and both the start warning and the streamed notice are still there, and it fails without the change. Unit tests in history-reconciliation.test.ts cover ordering and the no-warnings case (history is returned unchanged). Residual: the warnings aren't persisted, so reopening the session later from history (a fresh hydrate) won't show them. The start-of-session information is gone at that point, and a new session reports any plugin that still fails.

Valid. `sendPrompt` adds the optimistic user bubble before `startSession`, and `startSession` appends the plugin warning after it, so the backward search in the `chat_queued_prompt_start` handler stops at the warning and appends the prompt again. It's cosmetic and lasts until saved history replaces the live transcript. Fix: skip rows with `meta.messageKind === "plugin_issue"` in that loop. Will take it with the P1 fix.

[P2] Prevent a retired pane's failed send from overwriting the current draft

`setPromptInput` now writes this app-owned Map, but `ChatThreadPane.handleSend` still decides whether to restore a failed prompt using its own `promptInputRef` after `await sendPrompt` (page.tsx:1915–1923). Send in A with a slow session start/reattach, navigate to B and back to A, and type a newer draft before the original start fails. The old pane's ref is still empty, so its continuation writes the submitted prompt over the new pane's cached draft. The visible input still contains the newer text, but another navigation restores the old submitted text and loses the newer draft.

I reproduced this with the real `usePromptDraft` and a deferred rejection through the real `useChatSession`; I also executed the production `handleSend` extracted from page.tsx. Validate the current draft revision/thread lifetime before restoring, rather than relying on a retired instance's ref. Add a deferred-send regression across A → B → A and another remount; the newer draft must survive. The same guard should keep late recovery from reinserting a draft after its thread was deleted and pruned.
